sections.h2: What is Houma, and how is it governed?
sections.html:
Houma is the largest city in Terrebonne Parish and its parish seat, and since 1984 the city government has been folded into the Terrebonne Parish Consolidated Government. Permits, planning and most local services therefore come from the parish rather than a separate city hall.

Wikipedia lists the city as founded in the 1830s, incorporated in 1848 and reincorporated in 1898. It is the principal city of the Houma-Bayou Cane-Thibodaux metropolitan area. Bayou Cane, the largest neighboring community, is a separate census-designated place that locals often treat as part of Houma. Wikipedia notes that with the urbanized neighboring areas included, the total would exceed 60,000 residents.

The Census Bureau counted 33,406 people in the 2020 census and estimates 31,735 for July 1, 2025, a decline. The city covers 14.47 square miles of land. Main roads include US Route 90, which is slated to become Interstate 49, plus Louisiana 24, 311 and 182.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Houma housing?
sections.html:
Houma is mostly owner-occupied, with 72.4 percent of housing units owned and a median home value of $205,900 for 2020 to 2024. That value is close to Bossier City's and below Central's.

Measure (2020-2024)Houma
Owner-occupied housing unit rate72.4%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$205,900
Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage$1,548
Median monthly owner costs without a mortgage$449
Median gross rent$1,058
Households13,346
Persons per household2.41

Houma's population dropped from 33,406 in the 2020 census to 31,735 in the 2025 estimate. Citywide figures like these say little about any one street, so treat them as background rather than a price.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts for Houma.

sections.h2: How did Hurricane Ida affect Houma houses?
sections.html:
Hurricane Ida made landfall in southeast Louisiana on August 29, 2021, and Houma took the intense eye wall of the Category 4 storm. Wikipedia describes widespread damage, and a year later NBC News reported displacement and property damage still lingering.

FEMA's one-year summary gives the statewide scale: more than 564,000 individual assistance applications approved for over $1.2 billion, 14,540 flood insurance claims paid for more than $655 million and over 26,000 Small Business Administration disaster loan applications. Those are state totals, not Houma figures, but they show how large the repair and insurance process was.

For a seller whose house was hit, buyers tend to ask:

  • Was the roof replaced, and was the work permitted?
  • Was there wind-driven water inside the walls or attic?
  • Did an insurance or FEMA payment cover the repairs, and were the repairs finished?
  • Are there leftover blue tarps, rotted decking or mold?

An as-is buyer who does not need a lender's appraisal can often close despite open repairs, which is why damaged houses sometimes sell this way.

Sources: Wikipedia: Houma, FEMA: Hurricane Ida by the Numbers at One Year.

FEMA has been revising the flood maps for portions of Houma and unincorporated Terrebonne Parish, and the revised preliminary maps were released on October 8, 2021. FEMA's page was last updated on January 21, 2025.

The maps define Special Flood Hazard Areas, which FEMA describes as areas at high risk for flooding, and they set rates for flood insurance. FEMA says residents can look at them through the local floodplain administrator, the FEMA Map Service Center online, a Flood Map Changes Viewer or a Map Specialist at 1-877-FEMA-MAP (1-877-336-2627).

Preliminary maps are not final, so check the status for your address before telling a buyer what zone it is in. A seller can do three things:

  • Look up the effective map and any preliminary map for the address.
  • Keep any elevation certificate and flood insurance declarations page.
  • Be ready to say whether the house flooded in the past and how it was repaired.

Source: FEMA: Revised preliminary flood maps for Terrebonne Parish.

sections.h2: What weather does a Houma house have to withstand?
sections.html:
Houma is low and wet. Wikipedia lists the elevation at 10 feet above sea level and the 1991 to 2020 normals at 65.42 inches of rain a year, with July and August the wettest months at 9.06 and 6.50 inches.

Daily mean temperatures reach about 82.7 degrees in July and 82.9 in August, with record highs of 104. The record low is 5 degrees, set in February. That mix puts stress on roofs, siding and air conditioning, and a deep freeze can split exposed pipes in a house that has not seen one in years.

Buyers and inspectors will focus on roofing, drainage and moisture. Sellers who can show a recent roof, working gutters and a dry crawl space or slab edge usually face fewer price questions.

Source: Wikipedia: Houma, Louisiana.

sections.h2: Which industries keep Houma's housing market moving?
sections.html:
Houma's economy rests on energy, marine work, seafood and health care. The Terrebonne Parish Economic Development Authority calls the parish one of the leading regions for oil and gas production in the country, and says that industry sustains a large inland marine and port economy.

It also describes Terrebonne as a leader in shrimp, oyster and other aquaculture harvesting, with a significant base of sugar cane farming. Aviation supports about 750 jobs, plus 2,000 direct industrial jobs at the airport's industrial park, and health services employ about 7,000.

Energy employment moves with oil prices and offshore activity, which can leave a household with a house to sell on short notice after a layoff or a transfer. A buyer who can close on a firm date is useful in that situation.

Source: Terrebonne Parish Economic Development Authority.

sections.h2: How is a Houma sale recorded, and what does recording cost?
sections.html:
A Houma sale is recorded with the Terrebonne Parish Clerk of Court, and its fee schedule starts at $105 for one to five pages. The schedule posted by the clerk is dated August 1, 2017, so confirm the current figures before closing.

Document lengthFee, one index type
1 to 5 pages$105
6 to 25 pages$205
26 to 50 pages$305
51 or more pages$305 plus $5 per extra page

The fee includes up to 10 names indexed, a certified copy and the portal fee, and it is assessed separately for each recording book. Under the Louisiana Civil Code a sale of an immovable must be made by authentic act or by act under private signature, so the act of sale is signed before a notary and then recorded.

Sources: Terrebonne Parish Clerk recording fees, Civil Code art. 2440.

sections.h2: Which way of selling a Houma house makes sense?
sections.html:
The choice usually comes down to repairs, timing and who is paying for them. A cash sale as-is helps a house that still needs storm repairs or a roof, while a traditional listing may suit a finished house.

Louisiana's Act 807 of 2026 adds requirements for wholesaling residential real property, and the Real Estate Commission now publishes a mandatory cancellation notice. Ask any buyer whether they plan to assign your contract, and read the cancellation language first.

Source: Louisiana Real Estate Commission.

faqs.q: Is Houma its own city government?
faqs.a: Houma remains a city, but its government was absorbed by the parish in 1984. Planning and permits run through the Terrebonne Parish Consolidated Government.

faqs.q: What are Houma's flood maps doing?
faqs.a: FEMA released revised preliminary flood maps for portions of Houma and unincorporated Terrebonne Parish on October 8, 2021, and updated its page on January 21, 2025. Check the effective and preliminary status for your address with the local floodplain administrator or FEMA's Map Service Center.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded in Houma?
faqs.a: At the Terrebonne Parish Clerk of Court. The clerk's posted schedule lists $105 for one to five pages, including up to 10 names indexed, a certified copy and the portal fee, but it is dated 2017, so confirm current fees.

faqs.q: How many Houma homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports 72.4 percent of housing units are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024, with a median home value of $205,900. These are city-wide figures.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Houma house that still has Ida damage?
faqs.a: Yes, as-is sales are possible. Tell buyers what you know about the damage and keep insurance and repair records. A cash buyer is not working under a lender's repair conditions, which is why damaged houses are often sold this way.
